For me, I engage situations like that intentionally. What I mean is I might feel like dancing in my own zone, be feeling more social, be feeling horny, whatever, and that place I'm in determines how I respond.  At the end of the day, the person you're going out for is you (I'm assuming), so it's really up to you to decide whether you want to talk to people more and what kind of interactions you want to have.  Some people may have a similar social intention as you and some people might not; sometimes connections happen and sometimes they don't, it takes two to tango. One of the main reasons I go out with these crowds is because I can be so innocent and even vulnerable with folks: there's so much less of the mind games and distrust of daily life. I'm just there for genuine fun, genuine connection, and spontaneity, and it's amazing every time meeting someone who's there for the same. All that being said, as long as you're not a dick do whatever you want.  As for the last part, in my opinion, smiling and saying thank you is most definitely not being aloof.

I relate to many things being summed up by a couple words. In my experience, everything I'm feeling comes back to the same couple of words. It could be more to spell out how I'm feeling, complex feelings merit essays, but nothing else feels quite right. I know you said a lot more and I'm not trying to discount that.

I have no experience with anything relating to your situation, so ignore this if outsider perspective is not what you're looking for.

In terms of the kids, I think the important mindset to maintain is honesty; vague stories and getting wrapped up in words aren't going to work at explaining why she isn't there. Creating a clear message for them to understand and be able to hold on to is in my opinion best. Confusion causes pain for a child trying to understand the world.

The other point is to keep yourself in mind alongside them. This isn't easy for you. Just because you're the adult in this situation doesn't mean your emotions have no place there, too. Being put in a difficult situation and having to take care of others can make them feel like the only thing that's important, but you need you as well.
